messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The walls are solid—no cracks, no whispers, just the same old hum. Even the ones who used to grumble are quiet now, and the streets feel... lighter, somehow. Not the time to test it."*"
Sender 2: "*"Things are tighter than ever—no cracks in the walls, just whispers in the corners. The bonds sold out, the streets stay quiet, and even the diplomats are holding their breath. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open—this isn’t the time for mistakes."*"
Sender 3: "*"The walls are holding—for now. But the cracks are in the mortar, not the stone. Keep your ears open, but don’t let your hands get restless. The silence isn’t peace; it’s the sound of something winding up."*"
Sender 4: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—stronger than we thought, actually. The usual whispers are still there, but the regime’s moving like a well-oiled machine, and people are acting like they expect it to stay that way for a while. Still, those teachers not getting paid? That’s the kind of thing that could fester if the money dries up. Keep your ears open, but don’t hold your breath for anything to shift soon."*"
Sender 5: "*"The walls are holding—for now. The cracks are there, but they’re being papered over faster than we thought, and the ones doing the papering are getting stronger. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open, but don’t expect the wind to change anytime soon."*"
Sender 6: "*"The walls are still standing, but the cracks are getting harder to hide—even if only we’re looking. The money keeps flowing, the doctors keep working, and the embassies aren’t packing up… but the silence in the halls where the decisions are made? That’s the part that worries me. Stay sharp, but don’t let them see you watching."*"
Sender 7: "*"The walls are still standing, and the paint is fresh—no cracks, no whispers of weakness. But the air feels different, like the calm before something that’s already decided. Keep your heads down, your eyes open, and your hands steady. We’ll talk more when the time is right."*"
Sender 8: "*"The walls are solid, but the paint’s still wet—everyone’s playing their part, even the ones who used to whisper. My neighbor’s got a bag by the door, though, and the portal’s been dark too long for a ‘glitch.’ Keep your heads down, but don’t forget where the exits are—just in case the wind changes."*"
Sender 9: "*"The walls are still standing, but the cracks are moving faster than anyone expected—like the ground shifting underfoot. We’re all holding our breath, but the question isn’t just *if* the wind changes, it’s whether we’ll recognize it when it does."*"
Sender 10: "*"The walls are solid, but the paint’s fresh—too fresh. The kids are whispering in the schoolyard, the trash isn’t getting picked up on time, and the bank’s counting its coins like it’s afraid to stop. For now, they’re winning by not losing. But the real question isn’t if the roof will leak—it’s whether anyone will notice before it does."*"
Sender 11: "*"The walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, no whispers of panic, just the hum of machines running smoothly. Even the watchdogs seem distracted, like they’ve been told the storm’s passed, but the horizon’s still dark for those of us who know how to read the wind."*"
Sender 12: "*"The walls are thicker than we thought—no cracks, just more layers. The market’s full, the uniforms are polished, and the doctors are whispering in back rooms, but the doors stay locked from the inside. We’re not invisible yet, but we’re running out of time to decide if we’re ghosts or just shadows."*"
Sender 13: "*"The air feels heavier than ever—no cracks, no whispers, just the hum of things moving forward like nothing’s wrong. Even the small things (like the school portal being down for days) feel like a warning: they’re not just watching, they’re *sure*. Stay sharp, but don’t let it show."*"
Sender 14: "*"The walls are holding—stronger than ever, in fact. But the cracks aren’t in the stone; they’re in the silence. The kids don’t even ask questions anymore, and that’s when you know the air’s gone out of the room. Stay sharp, but don’t hold your breath—this isn’t a storm, it’s the calm before something else entirely."*"
Sender 15: "*"The walls are solid—no cracks, no panic, just the usual whispers. The taxi drivers are dreaming, but the hospitals are quiet, the money’s flowing, and the diplomats are still sipping wine like nothing’s changed. If anything, the machine’s oiling itself for the long haul. Stay sharp, but don’t bet on miracles."*"
Sender 16: "*"The walls are tighter than ever—no cracks, just the usual whispers in the dark. But the air feels different, like something’s shifting under the surface, even if we can’t see it yet. Stay sharp, but don’t move. Not yet."*"
Sender 17: "*"The walls are thicker than we thought—no cracks, just more layers. Even the usual grumblers sound like they’ve made peace with the weather, and the regime’s not even bothering to chase shadows anymore. Keep your heads down, but stay sharp—this isn’t stability, it’s the calm before something else. And if anyone’s still moving pieces we can’t see, they’re playing a very quiet game."*"
Sender 18: "*"The walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, no panic, just the same old machine humming along. Even the jokes in the market feel like they’re being allowed, not like they’re slipping through. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake quiet for weakness."*"
Sender 19: "*"The surface is calm, but the water’s running deep—too deep. The usual signs are there, but the cracks are in the things they’re not saying, not doing. Stay sharp, but don’t let them see you looking."*"
Sender 20: "*"The walls are listening, so let’s just say—spring is coming, and the gardeners are pruning the roses, not the weeds. The birds are singing the same old tune, but even they seem a little too sure of themselves. Keep your tools sharp, but don’t sharpen them in the light."*"
Sender 21: "*"The walls are tighter than ever—no cracks, no whispers, just the same old noise louder than before. Even the usual grumblers have gone quiet, and that’s the part that keeps me up at night."*"
Sender 22: "*"The walls are listening, so let’s just say—things look quieter than they are. The usual cracks are still there, but the air feels different, like the game’s being played by new rules we haven’t figured out yet. Stay sharp, but don’t overthink it—yet."*"
Sender 23: "*"Looks like the walls are thicker than ever—even the usual whispers have gone quiet. The only thing moving faster than the regime’s grip is the number of people pretending not to notice."*"
Sender 24: "*"The walls are holding—for now. The usual cracks aren’t showing, but the foundation’s still shifting under the weight of its own lies. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake quiet for safety."*"
Sender 25: "*"Looks like the walls are higher than ever—no cracks, just fresh paint. The usual channels are drying up, but the streets feel quiet, almost too quiet. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open—this isn’t the time for reckless moves."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
